name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: An ADNOC vessel was attacked in Hormuz on 17 Nov, with one missing and 11 injured; Hormuz traffic remains minimal
state: ADNOC Logistics & Services said one of its vessels was attacked while transiting Hormuz on 17 Nov; one crew member is missing and 11 were injured (The National, 18 Nov). Oman said on 18 Nov it evacuated 24 people from a burning tanker off Musandam (Gulf News). UKMTO reported the tanker On Phoenix hit by a projectile on 16 Nov, while Iran's claims of mine strikes remain unverified (Riviera). Windward counted four inbound and no outbound transits on 17 Nov under a US blockade.
for_you: Shipping and energy disruption in the Gulf tends to raise fuel, freight and delivery costs. Check FCDO travel advice before travelling to the region.

sources.title: The National — Adnoc L&S ship attacked in Strait of Hormuz with one crew member missing
Gulf News — Iran attacks Bahrain, ADNOC vessel hit in Hormuz

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
